problem.text: JIT installation needs native source files after installation, but the previous manifest explicitly included only Hadamard data.

reasoning.text: Adding recursive inclusion of the native extension tree supplies a packaging rule independent of whether setup.py constructs a precompiled extension.

impact.text: The change targets availability of JIT build inputs, not compiler flags, kernel behavior or dependency versions.

source_notes.text: Issue #6 is titled “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr'”; its reporter says they do not have AMD, and its traceback ends at assert len(sources) > 0 after exllamav3/ext.py calls load.

That report is plausibly related because its load call matches the inspected JIT loader and its empty-source assertion fits missing packaged sources. This does not establish that the commit addresses the ROCm warning or that the author linked the issue.

limitations: No distribution build, installation or native compilation was executed; actual archive and installed-package contents remain unverified.
There is no useful numerical scalar check for this manifest-only change. Packaging-tool behavior requires a build rather than arithmetic emulation.

chapters.title: Carry native sources into JIT installations

claims.text: MANIFEST.in retains include exllamav3/util/hadamard_data/* and adds recursive-include exllamav3/exllamav3_ext *. The wildcard covers the native tree rather than only compilation units, including nested headers and sources.

setup.py enables include_package_data and disables precompilation when EXLLAMA_NOCOMPILE is present. Its CUDAExtension configuration exists only when precompilation is enabled and Torch is available; otherwise setup_kwargs is empty.

At runtime, ext.py first imports exllamav3_ext. On ModuleNotFoundError it recursively discovers .c, .cpp and .cu files beneath the installed Python module's exllamav3_ext directory, then passes them to torch.utils.cpp_extension.load with that directory as an include path.

The broad recursive rule preserves both translation units and supporting headers without maintaining a second extension-specific file list. Its tradeoff is including the whole native subtree rather than narrowly selecting build inputs. Precompilation remains the existing alternative; neither build path's implementation changes.

annotation.summary: Explicitly includes the native extension tree in the package manifest so JIT installations can retain sources and headers needed by the runtime loader.
